# Runtime I/O units

`distance` and `mass` are the simulation length and mass units (for example centimeters and kilograms); `sec`, `deg` and `rad` mean seconds, degrees and radians. Angular joint columns use degrees; rigid-body angular values and inverse-dynamics inputs use radians. These are runtime values, not population scaling instructions.

Conditional units depend on the live axis, drive, material or tendon gearing. Packed values list their component units in order.

## Dimensionless

dimensionless.

## Not applicable

not applicable.

## Length

distance.

## Mass

mass.

## Inverse mass

1 / mass.

## Time

sec.

## Velocity

distance / sec.

## Acceleration

distance / sec^2.

## Angle

rad.

## Angular velocity

rad / sec.

## Angular acceleration

rad / sec^2.

## Force

mass * distance / sec^2.

## Torque

mass * distance^2 / sec^2.

## Impulse

mass * distance / sec.

## Inertia

mass * distance^2.

## Inverse inertia

1 / (mass * distance^2).

## Pressure

mass / (distance * sec^2).

## Linear stiffness

mass / sec^2.

## Linear damping

mass / sec.

## Joint coordinate

Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | deg |
| Linear | distance |

## Joint rate

Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | deg / sec |
| Linear | distance / sec |

## Joint effort

Generalized effort is torque on rotational axes and force on translational axes; it receives no degree conversion.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | mass * distance^2 / sec^2 |
| Linear | mass * distance / sec^2 |

## Joint stiffness

The SDK gain is per rad or per rad/sec. The runtime converts the denominator to deg for angular columns, including acceleration drives; it does not convert the output acceleration numerator. Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular force drive | mass * distance^2 / (sec^2 * deg) |
| Linear force drive | mass / sec^2 |
| Angular acceleration drive | rad / (deg * sec^2) |
| Linear acceleration drive | 1 / sec^2 |

## Joint damping

The SDK gain is per rad or per rad/sec. The runtime converts the denominator to deg for angular columns, including acceleration drives; it does not convert the output acceleration numerator. Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular force drive | mass * distance^2 / (sec * deg) |
| Linear force drive | mass / sec |
| Angular acceleration drive | rad / (deg * sec) |
| Linear acceleration drive | 1 / sec |

## Joint armature

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | mass * distance^2 |
| Linear | mass |

## Effort per rate

Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | mass * distance^2 / (sec * deg) |
| Linear | mass / sec |

## Rate per effort

Angular joint columns use degrees in both reads and writes; linear columns use distance.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Angular | deg * sec / (mass * distance^2) |
| Linear | sec / mass |

## Jacobian

Maps generalized velocities to link linear and angular velocities. Angular columns use rad/sec, including floating-base rotation; linear columns use distance/sec. No degree conversion.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Linear row linear column | dimensionless |
| Linear row angular column | distance / rad |
| Angular row linear column | rad / distance |
| Angular row angular column | dimensionless |

## Mass matrix

Maps generalized accelerations to force/torque. Angular accelerations use rad/sec^2, with radians dimensionless in the mechanical mass/inertia units. No degree conversion.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Linear row linear column | mass |
| Linear row angular column | mass * distance |
| Angular row linear column | mass * distance |
| Angular row angular column | mass * distance^2 |

## Centroidal momentum matrix

The matrix maps generalized velocities to linear/angular momentum; its final column is a bias force/torque for the momentum derivative, not momentum. Angular velocities use rad/sec, with radians dimensionless in the mechanical mass/inertia units. No degree conversion.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Linear row linear column | mass |
| Linear row angular column | mass * distance |
| Angular row linear column | mass * distance |
| Angular row angular column | mass * distance^2 |
| Linear row bias | mass * distance / sec^2 |
| Angular row bias | mass * distance^2 / sec^2 |

## Tendon coordinate

Fixed-tendon length is offset + sum(SDK coefficient * SDK joint position). For revolute axes, parsing and gearing updates multiply authored gearing by rad-to-deg, so unit authored gearing yields degrees. Mixed axes or dimensionful gearing determine their own common coordinate unit.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Unit authored gearing angular | deg |
| Unit authored gearing linear | distance |

## Tendon stiffness

For arbitrary fixed-tendon coefficients, joint effort = stiffness * coordinate error * reciprocalCoefficient. Both position and force coefficients determine the unit; mixed-axis configurations require their declared coefficient units. The angular variant assumes unit authored gearing and unit force coefficient; the SDK gearing includes rad-to-deg.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Unit authored gearing angular | mass * distance^2 / (sec^2 * deg) |
| Unit authored gearing linear | mass / sec^2 |

## Tendon damping

For arbitrary fixed-tendon coefficients, joint effort = damping * tendon coordinate rate * reciprocalCoefficient. Both position and force coefficients determine the unit; mixed-axis configurations require their declared coefficient units. The angular variant assumes unit authored gearing and unit force coefficient; the SDK gearing includes rad-to-deg.

| Case | Units |
|---|---|
| Unit authored gearing angular | mass * distance^2 / (sec * deg) |
| Unit authored gearing linear | mass / sec |

## Wrench

force xyz: mass * distance / sec^2; torque xyz: mass * distance^2 / sec^2; application point xyz: distance.

Component units: mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2, distance, distance, distance.

## Ground plane

normal xyz: dimensionless; plane distance: distance.

Component units: dimensionless, dimensionless, dimensionless, distance.

## Kinematic target

position xyz: distance; active flag w: dimensionless.

Component units: distance, distance, distance, dimensionless.

## Spatial force

force xyz: mass * distance / sec^2; torque xyz: mass * distance^2 / sec^2.

Component units: mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2, mass * distance^2 / sec^2.

## Culling box write

enable flag: dimensionless; min/max xyz: distance.

Seven scalar elements: enable (0 to clear, 1 to store), min x/y/z, max x/y/z. Readback contains only the six distance values.

Component units: dimensionless, distance, distance, distance, distance, distance, distance.
